---
title: "Check the playbook applies"
description: "Check the playbook applies, and how to treat your kind of work."
---

The playbook applies if both of these are true:

1. You collected, manipulated or interpreted data to answer a question.
2. Somebody is going to act on the answer.

This includes any [analytical output](../09-resources/r1-glossary.qmd) used internally, supplied to a sponsor or published externally.

If it applies, start at [Phase 1, engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd).

## Find your kind of work

[Decide your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) for your own work. Do not match it to the nearest row. The second column is an example, not your score.

| The work | Example impact, or how to treat it | What else applies |
|------------------------------|------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| Exploratory analysis, an internal data investigation | Impact 1 | Level 1 requires separation within your team. See [deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) |
| A monthly operational dashboard, team workforce planning | Impact 2 | Do the [checks for your level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/what-your-level-requires.qmd#the-checks-by-level). Read [Phase 5, review](../05-review/index.qmd) for what a recurring output is reviewed against, and when |
| An official statistics publication, such as Dental Statistics | Impact 3 | Ask the Lead Official for Statistics for advice ([who to ask](../09-resources/r3-who-to-ask.qmd)). Read [what the Code of Practice for Statistics asks for](../09-resources/r9-what-each-standard-asks-for.qmd#the-code-of-practice-for-statistics) |
| A Freedom of Information (FOI) response, or a Parliamentary Question | Impact 3 | Score visibility under public visibility and reach. Do not add it on top. See [score the impact](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/score-the-impact.qmd) |
| A Board report or a ministerial briefing | Impact 3 | Do not score Level 4 on visibility alone. See [what does not justify Level 4](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/score-the-impact.qmd#what-does-not-by-itself-justify-level-4) |
| A funding allocation formula, an eligibility model, a payment methodology, a major policy appraisal | Impact 4, so Level 4 BCA | Follow [Business Critical analysis](../08-business-critical/index.qmd). Make the register entry and name the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer at scoping |
| A dataset supplied to a sponsor or a partner | Score it like any other analysis | The playbook applies when you supply it, not only when you publish it |
| A forecasting model informing budgets | Score it, then place it among the eight model types | See [deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) for both. Read [uncertainty, assumptions and limitations](../09-resources/r10-uncertainty.qmd) |
| An algorithmic or machine learning tool that affects decisions about people | Score it, and separately check transparency scope | Check transparency scope at scoping, with the impact score. [Algorithmic transparency and AI](../09-resources/r12-algorithmic-transparency-and-ai.qmd) has the test |
| An AI assistant helping you write code, summarise or draft | Nothing changes about who is accountable | Ask before you use a tool that is not already in use in your team.<br><br>Do not put data into a tool that is not cleared to hold it.<br><br>Verify what comes back.<br><br>Record material use where it affects reproducibility.<br><br>See [using AI tools to do the analysis](../09-resources/r12-algorithmic-transparency-and-ai.qmd#using-ai-tools-to-do-the-analysis) for all five rules |
| Analysis you are reusing for a new purpose, or a one-off that has become a monthly production run | Check whether the original level still holds | Check four things before reuse and score the level again if any answer is yes. See [Phase 5, review](../05-review/index.qmd).<br><br>Treat a one-off that becomes a production run as a different piece of work and score it again |
| A published figure that has turned out to be wrong | Not a new piece of analysis | Decide whether it is a revision or a correction.<br><br>Grade a correction by what it does to the conclusions already drawn: significant, minor but significant, or minor but insignificant.<br><br>See [correcting a published figure](../09-resources/r6-when-something-is-wrong.qmd) for what happens at each grade |
| Work where there is not enough time for the assurance the level asks | The level does not change | Narrow the question, or state plainly what assurance was not done. See [after you have your level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/after-you-have-your-level.qmd) |

: Kinds of work, how each is treated, and what else applies to it
